free_tier.stated: A container-based Linux root server, free while renewed by hand each month: 'The model "VS2-free" can be used free of charge in the basic version with IPv6 and is ideal for testing, as a development environment or as the basis for creating larger and growing systems.' Spec, quoted: 'Frequency 1 Core @ 1 GHz', 'Virtualization Type Linux Container', 'RAM 1 GB', 'Harddisk 10 GB HDD @ Raid10', 'Network-Card 1x 1Gbit', 'monthly included traffic volume 1 TB'. One IPv6 /128 is included; the IPv4 row is a dash, so the free model ships no IPv4 at all.
free_tier.notes: perpetual-renewable, not perpetual: free only while the customer renews it monthly

retention.stated: One month, renewed by hand. The vendor's own forum answers the question directly: asked 'I need to perform a renew action by hand every month?', the support account replies 'yes.'; asked 'Can this be handled automatically?', 'no'; asked 'What happens when I forget this?', 'server becomes down'; asked 'That incurs again a payment?', 'no until offer is valid.' Extension now requires an emailed PIN: 'since the extension of a VS2free server has now verification PINs that we send by email'.

egress.terms: 'Traffic | monthly included traffic volume | 1 TB', and above it: 'If the inclusive traffic is exceeded, the connection becomes capped to 1Mbit/s, if no additional traffic is purchased by customer'

chaining: 1 GB of RAM with full root and 1 TB of traffic is the largest permanent free general-purpose machine found, and because it is a Linux container it can run rclone, a crawler or an SSH tunnel from an IPv6-capable peer.

identity_cost.detail: No card and no hold: the free model is ordered without payment. The live registration form requires 'Email Address *', 'PIN for Email Validation *', 'Customer Type' (Private or Corporate), 'Salutation *', 'First Name *', 'Last Name *', 'Country *', 'Date of Birth (DD.MM.YYYY) *' and 'Password *'; a company name and a VAT-ID are optional ('VAT-ID (only for EU-Companies) (optional)'). The country list carries 252 entries including 'United States', 'China' and 'Taiwan, Province Of China', so a non-EU signup is offered. The postal address and phone are NOT on the registration form; they are filled in afterwards in the customer panel, and third-party guides report the order only becomes effective once they are. No ID document is requested anywhere read. Nothing was signed up for.

reliability_note: no reliability event observed. The known failure mode is procedural and stated by the vendor: a missed monthly renewal takes the server down, and the renewal needs a reachable email address to receive the PIN.

notes: VERIFIED 2026-10-24, and this record's own notes were wrong. They said 'Not in the corpus: `ls dossier/compute | grep -i euserv` returns nothing' - but this file exists, and so does euserv-vs2-free.json. The same product is recorded twice under two slugs with different URLs; The product is real and orderable. Three corrections. (1) It is NOT permanent: one-month contract, manual renewal, vendor answers 'yes' to renewing by hand and 'server becomes down' if you forget. (2) The free model includes NO IPv4 - the row is a dash - and IPv4 is a paid add-on ('additional IPv4 | EUR per IP / mo | yes, optional up to 16'). The price is a dash because the page renders it client-side from an endpoint that returned the same figure for every row id tried, so it could not be attributed to the IPv4 row. (3) Registration asks for a date of birth and a country, not a postal address or phone; those are entered afterwards in the customer panel. No ID document is requested. Signup: https://www.euserv.com/en/register.php, then the order link on the product page.
